title: Light Agents inherit GovOps benefits from a parent Agent's Executor Accord but get no direct Primitive access
content:
A.2.2.6.3 defines the Light Agent Primitive as enabling "Light Agents, which are sub-agents operating on top of the Agent's Executor Accord, conferring the advantages of Sky GovOps at a lower cost, but **without direct access to other Sky Primitives**."

The trade is explicit and clean. What a Light Agent gets is the expensive part to reproduce — an operational relationship with GovOps actors, inherited rather than negotiated, since it rides on a parent's existing Accord. What it gives up is the Primitive surface: no SkyLink, no Allocation System, no Distribution Reward of its own.

This creates a genuine tier below full Agent status. Read against the Agent formation pipeline — capital deployment, creation fee, Scaffold Artifact, Transformation, token launch, Accord negotiation, Root Edit governance setup — the cost of becoming a Prime Agent is substantial, and Light Agents are the answer for activity that cannot justify it.

The structural consequence is that Primitive access remains the defining privilege of full Agent status, and the ecosystem can grow its actor count without proportionally growing the set of entities holding permissioned protocol access. Accountability also stays concentrated: a Light Agent's operational conduct runs through its parent's Accord, so the parent's Executor relationship is what backs it.
description: A cheaper derivative tier: sub-agents ride on an existing Accord to obtain Sky GovOps advantages, while the Primitive surface stays reserved for full Agents.
